Newsstand, iOS 5 and 6

A special iOS folder that showed downloaded magazines and newspapers on wooden shelves.

Source
Wikipedia: Newsstand (software)
Creator
Apple
Made
Introduced with iOS 5 (October 2011); shelves replaced in iOS 7
Style
Skeuomorphism (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Familiar, warm, crafted
Evidence
Inspected a 960 px copy of File:Apple Newsstand on iOS 6 on an iPhone 3GS.jpg (Delicje, 2021, CC BY-SA 4.0), a slightly blurred photo of the empty Newsstand folder on iOS 6. Not stored.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Newsstand “emulated a newsagent’s shop, with virtual shelves that held and presented each newspaper and magazine that had been downloaded.” It was “a visual shelf accessible directly on the iOS home screen, similar in style to iBooks,” available from iOS 5. Wikipedia: Newsstand (software)).

Observed

  • The open folder shows two shelves of pale, grained wood with a light front lip.
  • A pale header strip carries the name “Newsstand” in dark bold type and a small beveled “Store” button.
  • The Newsstand icon is a small set of empty wooden shelves in a rounded square.
  • An empty-state message sits on the shelf as a pale blue card.

Why it belongs

A folder with no physical counterpart is given one: a shop shelf. The material carries the meaning, so the wood covers the full width.

Borrow

Show an empty collection as an empty shelf with a single card on it.
